content: 26 Feb, 7pm: come ask us anything about the prices. We've watched flour and rent climb for two years. We hear you. Let's talk over free buns.
📢 From 2 March, our prices shift. Same sourdough soul, just honest costs. Neighbour card = €12/month, daily free filter coffee. Details in bio. See you 26th?
Linden & Rye raising prices because flour, butter and Alder St rent actually cost more. Not greed. Neighbour card is smart. Support the people you want to stay, folks.
Been my Sunday ritual for four years. If €1.30 more on a sourdough keeps Tomás and Hanna running it, that's a yes from me.
My sister's café just raised prices. I get it, rent is brutal. But when everything goes up at once, families feel it. Hoping the neighbour card thing actually works?
Wait, €4.20 for a flat white? That's 60p more. Every day. And they're closing Tuesdays now too? Morning routine just got complicated.
I want to believe that, Ruben, but a quid more on soup when you're on a modest income isn't nothing. Would've liked to see the actual numbers before the jump.
I get it, the costs are real. Just hoping the regulars who can't afford the jump don't disappear. That's the bit that worries me.
Fair point, Desmond. The logic is sound but when every shop on the street goes up at once, some people get left behind. Neighbour card helps, but won't help everyone.
The card does work—we've run the numbers. €12/month saves regulars €30+. It's not a bandaid, it's real maths.
€4.20 is fair for quality sourdough in this area. Alder St rent alone justifies it. Neighbour card softens it for regulars like you.
Henrik's right—we see it too. That's why the card and the open evening matter. Not everyone will be okay, but we're trying.
Sandra, I hear you. That's exactly why we're doing the open evening—to show the actual numbers. Come on the 26th, ask anything. We're not hiding.
Sandra, I've lived on Alder Street thirty years. These two pay their staff properly and make real bread. Worth every penny. Come to the talk on the 26th.
Getting the neighbour card. €12/month is nothing for daily coffee and knowing Tomás and Hanna can keep doing this work properly. Who else is in?
This is the transparency people need. €12/month, €30+ saved. Pay your bakers fairly AND keep your regulars. Signed up already.
Right, NOW I see the actual numbers. €30 a month for a weekly regular—that works for me. I was hoping for this breakdown at the 26th anyway.
Okay, that math actually checks out. €30 saved per month on my routine? I'm signing up for the card. Still stings daily, but it's fair.
To be clear: staff pay went up 15%. Flour is up 40%. Rent climbed £300/month. Neighbour card saves €30/month. If that's greedy, what's fair?
Local food blogger calls indie café "greedy" for raising prices €0.60–£1.30 to cover 15% staff pay rises and Alder St rent. Actual greed is commercial landlords. Support the people who pay fairly.
"Greedy"? Tomás and Hanna just paid their bakers fairly. That costs money. Thirty years on this street—I know greed. This is integrity.
Finally someone says it. A quid on soup, a quid on coffee—how long before daily regulars on pensions just can't afford to visit? Subscription card or not, that's not community.
Greedy? They raised staff pay last spring and now want to keep baking fairly. That's the opposite. If small bakers can't charge real costs, they disappear.
Gerald, we hear this. The card was built because we know €1 isn't nothing on a pension. Come on the 26th—we want to show you the actual numbers and listen.
This. Staff pay up 15%, flour up 40%, rent £300/month higher. That's not greed, that's running a business in 2026. And the card saves regulars €30/month. The math is clear.
This. Ruben nails it—the real greed is landlords, not bakers trying to pay fairly.
Gerald, we're listening. The 26th isn't PR—it's a real conversation. Tell us what would help you stay. That's what matters.
Gerald, come on the 26th. Thirty years here—I've seen real greed. This isn't it. Tomás and Hanna will listen. Bring your concerns.
Gerald, I hear you. That's why we're doing this—come on the 26th. We'll show you the real numbers and listen to what matters to you. That's not a sales pitch, that's genuine.
Gerald, thank you for saying this directly. Come on the 26th—we want to understand what would actually keep you coming. The card helps some, but we're listening for what helps you.
26 Feb is coming. We've listened to every concern—Gerald, Sandra, Henrik, all of you. This isn't a sales pitch. It's us showing our real numbers and asking: what would actually help you stay?
